t:
The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that—
    (1) minting and issuing coins under this Act will not result in any net cost to the United States Government; and 
    (2) no funds, including applicable surcharges, shall be disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7 until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping) is recovered by the United States Treasury, consistent with sections 5112(m) and 5134(f) of title 31, United States Code.

fable.w: This is a financial-assurances provision for a commemorative coin program. It directs the Secretary to ensure there is no net cost to the government and that costs are recovered before surcharges are disbursed. The tempting reading is that the reference to a 'recipient designated in section 7' brings in an outside party, but that recipient only receives funds and has no consultative role in any federal decision. The section provides for no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that—

qwen_block.w: This section imposes financial constraints on the Secretary regarding the minting of coins, specifically ensuring no net cost to the government and recovering costs before disbursing funds. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The 'recipient' mentioned is the beneficiary of a disbursement, not a participant in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that— (1) minting and issuing coins under this Act will not result in any net cost to the United States Government; and (2) no funds, including applicable surcharges, shall be disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7 until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping) is recovered by the United States Treasury

opus.w: This section only tells the Secretary to make sure the coin program costs the government nothing, and that no surcharge money is paid out until costs are recovered. It doesn't create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty or right to sue. The outside recipient is only on the receiving end of a payment, which is like a benefit, not a role in the Secretary's decision.
opus.s: no funds, including applicable surcharges, shall be disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7 until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act
opus.b: This section is a standard "no net cost" rule for commemorative coins. The tempting-but-wrong reading is that the "recipient designated in section 7" is an outside party involved in a federal decision. That reading fails because the recipient only receives surcharge money after costs are recovered. It has no role in consulting on, advising on, or challenging the Secretary's decisions, and receiving funds is like a benefit, which doesn't count.

qwen_chat.w: The section outlines financial constraints and internal government procedures regarding the minting of coins and the disbursement of funds. It does not require or recommend consultation, coordination, or participation with any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The 'recipients' mentioned are only referenced in the context of a payment condition, not as participants in a decision.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "recipients designated in section 7" are outside parties and that the condition on disbursing funds to them constitutes a form of participation or consultation. However, the text does not describe any process of consulting, coordinating with, or hearing from these recipients before a decision is made. It merely sets a financial precondition for payment. Furthermore, the primary actors mentioned (Secretary, US Government, US Treasury) are all inside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes.
